structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Broad embedded portfolio and internal manufacturing/assembly capacity provide control, while external foundry/raw-material and demand dependencies remain.

structural-causal.name: supplyChainResilience
structural-causal.basis: Microchip operates internal assembly/test in Thailand and the Philippines and also uses outsourced capacity; diversification adds flexibility but creates geographic and supplier dependencies.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Embedded control is pervasive across physical infrastructure, but semiconductor cycles and inventory corrections can overwhelm secular demand for periods.

discovery-weak-signals.name: sales recovery
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Reported revenue grew materially from a depressed comparison base.

discovery-weak-signals.name: inventory normalization
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Company reported improving inventory conditions and book-to-bill above 1.

adversarial-red-team.name: financingResilience
adversarial-red-team.basis: June 30 2026 debt totaled about $5.4B and the company expects to refinance near-term maturities using debt, converts, revolver, commercial paper or other instruments.

adversarial-red-team.name: cycleRisk
adversarial-red-team.basis: Inventory days improved, but absolute inventory was roughly flat and demand normalization is not yet proven.

expectations-execution.name: cycle execution
expectations-execution.basis: Sales and margin recovery are visible while durability is not yet established.
